items.entity: Supports of the Fig. 3 row-1 instance (how many, points or segments, where)
items.description: Sec. 4.1 only describes the random generator: 1–4 constraints, each either a fixed point at a corner or edge midpoint, or a fixed segment 'connecting these locations'. It is unclear whether a segment is a half edge, a full edge or some other connection. The supports used for row 1 can only be seen in Fig. 3, whose caption gives only DiT settings. No sample index is given, and the dataset is only 'available on request'. A single isolated fixed point would leave a rigid-body rotation, so row 1 must have at least 2 points or a segment.
readings: Two left corners fixed as points: (0,0) and (0,L)
Lower half of left edge fixed: segment (0,0)-(0,0.5L)
Left- and right-edge midpoints fixed: (0,0.5L) and (L,0.5L)

items.entity: Restrained displacement components at each support
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says 'fixed points' and 'fixed segments', and the Fig. 1 caption says only 'Dirichlet boundary condition'. The text never says whether both u_x and u_y are restrained or whether some constraints are single-component rollers. The support symbols in Fig. 3 cannot be seen.
readings: Both u_x and u_y = 0 at every constrained node (pinned/clamped)
Some supports restrain only one component (roller, e.g. u_y = 0 only)

items.description: Sec. 4.1 says 'fixed points in the corners or midpoints of edges' but does not say whether a point support is one FE node or a small group of edge nodes around that location. This changes the local load path near the support.
readings: Single node at the corner or edge midpoint (e.g. node 32 of 0-64)
Patch of 3 consecutive edge nodes centred on the location
Short fixed segment about 2-4 elements long

items.entity: Application point of the single load in row 1
items.description: Sec. 4.1 only says 'A single external load was applied along the edge of the domain'. The edge and the position along it for row 1 are shown only in Fig. 3. The text also leaves open two things: (a) which positions were allowed (any boundary node including corners, or a restricted set), and (b) the origin, y-orientation and units of (x_load, y_load) in Eq. 25 (node index, pixel index or normalized; image y-down or y-up). Positions below use origin at bottom-left, y up.

items.entity: Direction of the unit load in row 1
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says the unit load has 'a direction sampled randomly'. The row-1 angle is shown only by the arrow in Fig. 3 (not visible). The text also does not say whether angles were drawn continuously or from a discrete set, or whether loads could point out of the domain.
readings: Arbitrary angle theta read from the Fig. 3 arrow, F = (cos theta, sin theta)

items.entity: How the load is spread spatially
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says the load was 'applied along the edge of the domain'. This could mean a concentrated nodal force, which fits the single coordinate pair in Eq. 25, or a load spread over part of the edge. If the coordinates are pixel-based, the load could also be split over the two nodes of one boundary element edge.
readings: Concentrated force at a single boundary node
Force split equally between the 2 nodes of one boundary element edge
Force distributed uniformly over a short edge segment (3-5 nodes)

items.entity: Target volume fraction f of row 1
items.description: Sec. 4.1 only says f is drawn per sample from a uniform distribution on [0.3, 0.5]. The row-1 value is not in the text. It could only be read from Fig. 3, if it is printed there at all.

items.entity: Young's modulus E0 of the solid
items.description: Eq. 2 introduces E0, but no value is given anywhere. With a unit load it only scales the compliance.
Poisson's ratio is never stated (Secs. 2 and 4.1). It enters the element stiffness and therefore the optimal layout.
Plane stress vs. plane strain is never stated for the 2D square domain (Sec. 4.1). The choice changes the effective constitutive matrix.

items.entity: Void stiffness Emin, density lower bound rho_min, and SIMP variant
items.description: Eq. 2 uses modified SIMP, E = Emin + rho^p (E0 - Emin), with Emin not given. Eq. 8 gives the classic-SIMP sensitivity -p rho^(p-1) U_e^T K_e U_e, with no (E0 - Emin) factor. Eq. 9 also clips to a lower bound rho_min whose value is not given. The interpolation variant and the void stiffness or lower bound are therefore inconsistent and undetermined.
readings: Classic SIMP: E = rho^3 E0 with rho_min = 1e-3

items.description: No filter type, filter radius or projection is mentioned anywhere. Sec. 2 uses raw sensitivities (Eq. 8). On a 64x64 grid, filtering strongly controls member thickness and checkerboarding.
readings: Sensitivity or density filter, rmin = 2-3 elements

items.entity: OC update parameters (move limit m, damping eta)
items.description: Eq. 10 lists 'm, eta > 0' but gives no values. As written, m multiplies B_e, so it would be absorbed into lambda and there would be no move limit; Eq. 9 has no +/- m bounds either. Sec. 2 also calls the scheme 'gradient descent'. Because the run stops at a fixed 100 iterations, these settings change the final design.
readings: Standard OC: move limit m = 0.2, eta = 0.5
Literal Eq. 9-10: no move limit, eta = 0.5

items.description: Sec. 4.1 says '100 optimization steps as the stopping criterion'. Sec. 2 says to stop when the relative compliance change falls below 'a specified tolerance' or when the maximum number of iterations is reached. The tolerance is never given, and it is unclear whether an early stop was active.
readings: At most 100 iterations, stop if relative compliance change < 1e-3
At most 100 iterations, stop if max density change < 0.01

items.description: The SIMP starting design is not stated. Sec. 4.1 mentions the 'initial domain assuming full material presence', but only for computing the conditioning stress/strain fields. Since the run is cut off at 100 iterations, the starting design can affect the result.

items.entity: Thresholding of the final SIMP design into the binary topology map
items.description: Sec. 2 says 'a thresholding step is applied to eliminate any remaining intermediate densities', and Sec. 4.1 stores 'a binary topology map'. The threshold value or rule is not given. It determines the binary SIMP design shown in Fig. 3 and its actual volume fraction.
readings: Volume-preserving threshold (keep the f*4096 densest elements)

items.description: Secs. 4.1 and 4.2 only say '64x64 square elements' on a uniform grid. The element type and integration rule are not stated.

items.entity: Physical side length and out-of-plane thickness of the square domain
items.description: Only the element count (64x64, Sec. 4.1) is given; the side length L (element size) and the thickness t are not. With a unit point load on square bilinear elements, these only scale the compliance (or leave it unchanged).
The text never says whether any elements are forced solid or void, for example pads at the load point or along supports. 'None' is the likely default, but it is not stated.
readings: Small solid pad of elements at the load point
Solid elements along fixed support segments

locator: Sec. 5, Fig. 3, row 1 (the first dataset instance shown with a SIMP design)
